text:
maria_cs: Heads-up — Ledgerly reported a significant behavior change after last night's model rollout (redwood-m-1.2). Their invoices are missing line-items and some fields are being redacted. They gave a repro and are escalated to P1.

lucy_support: Oh no — they noticed it in production after ~200 requests, mostly for invoice parsing use-case. Customer-facing example in thread: `invoice_total` present but `line_items` empty.

maria_cs: Repro snippet they provided (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood-m-1.2", "input": "Extract line items from invoice:\nInvoice #12345\nItems:\n- Widget A $12.00 x2\n- Widget B $5.00 x1" }
```
Response: `{"invoice_total":"29.00","line_items":[]}`

omar_eng: Thanks — initial guess is a safety filter or tokenizer change in 1.2 that treats certain dash-prefixed lists as potential PII and redacts them to `[]`. I'm spinning up a quick reproduce on canary.

ryan_sre: FYI we saw a small latency spike on canary for short sequences after the batching tweak; might be related but not sure. No 5xx.

maria_cs: Customer is asking for immediate mitigation steps and ETA for a fix. What can we offer now?

omar_eng: Short-term mitigations:
1) Pin them to previous model: `redwood-m-1.1` (recommended) — fastest.
2) As a temporary server-side patch: add header `X-RW-Model-Fallback: redwood-m-1.1` to their route to force fallback on mismatch.
3) If they can't switch, increase `top_p` or `temperature` to make the model less conservative — but that may change other outputs.

lucy_support: I can push step 1 for them if engineering approves. Ledgerly has strict SLAs so they want a rollback now.

omar_eng: We should pause the global rollout of 1.2 canaries immediately until we understand if this is a systemic safety redaction change. I'll open a rollback PR for the canary bucket.

deploy-bot: [deploy] Pausing rollout for release/redwood-m-1.2 -> canary pool A (triggered by omar_eng at 2026-03-17T11:24:35Z).

ryan_sre: I'll also run a quick diff of tokenization boundaries between 1.1 and 1.2 on the invoice samples. If it's a safety classifier threshold change we can roll a config patch faster than a model re-release.

maria_cs: Communication plan for customer: Lucy, can you send this to Ledgerly? Keep it short: acknowledge, mitigation (pin to 1.1), ETA for next update (we'll confirm within 90 minutes).

lucy_support: Draft to customer: "Thanks — we see this. We're temporarily pinning your traffic to redwood-m-1.1 and pausing the 1.2 rollout. Expect confirmation within 90 minutes. We're investigating cause and will share next steps." Sending now.

omar_eng: Quick repro steps for eng: curl snippet to reproduce and logs we need:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-m-1.2","input":"<sanitized invoice>"}'
```
Please collect runtime logs: `runtime.request_id`, `safety.filter_score`, `tokenization.boundaries` for the request.

ryan_sre: Collected logs from canary run: safety.filter_score spiked to 0.97 on line-item tokens for a bunch of samples. On 1.1 the score was 0.12. That points to a classifier/regression in the safety layer.

omar_eng: Confirmed — safety model update shipped with 1.2 accidentally tightened the PII/redaction threshold for list-like tokens. Short-term fix: revert safety config to previous thresholds and deploy. I'll push a config rollback to config-service now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] Rolling back safety-config v2026-03-17T02 to v2026-03-16T18 on canary cluster (started by omar_eng).

lucy_support: Ledgerly replied — "thank you, pinning works and invoice line-items are back for our sample checks." They asked: will this affect other customers?

maria_cs: We'll send a follow-up to the affected customers: explanation + steps we took + advisory to pin to 1.1 if they prefer. Also offer to run a couple of their samples.

omar_eng: Status update for the thread:
- 11:24 — Pause 1.2 rollout (canary).
- 11:26 — Pinned Ledgerly to 1.1.
- 11:32 — Identified safety threshold regression (safety.filter_score).
- 11:45 — Rolled back safety-config on canary.
- 11:52 — Confirmed Ledgerly sample fixed.

ryan_sre: Monitoring: I'm watching canary traffic for similar spikes. If we see re-occurrence we will fully rollback 1.2 across canary pools.

maria_cs: Next actions:
- Omar: follow up with runtime/research on why safety model parameters changed in 1.2 build and create a new test case for invoice-like lists.
- Ryan: keep monitoring, run a quick scan for other customers that recently started 1.2.
- Lucy: send a customer note with the actions and offer to re-run their regression test set.

omar_eng: Will do. Also adding an automated regression test to CI to catch this exact tokenization+filter threshold combination.

lucy_support: Ledgerly asked for a public postmortem or at least a short incident blurb. We'll draft a short-ops note once engineering confirms root cause.

maria_cs: Great. For now, marking this as P1 in the customer escalation tracker. I'll update the ticket with the pinned model and the steps taken.

deploy-bot: [ticket] Escalation P1 updated: pinned_model=redwood-m-1.1, mitigation=rollback_safety_config, status=monitoring.

omar_eng: ETA for full fix (safe release of 1.2 variant): dependent on retrain/tune of safety classifier — estimate 24-48 hours. Will post updates in this thread.

maria_cs: Thanks all. I'll close the loop with Ledgerly and ask for any additional samples. Keep this thread for updates.

ryan_sre: 12:10 — monitoring shows no new high safety scores after rollback. I'll reopen if anything changes.

maria_cs: 12:20 — Ledgerly confirmed through their automated test set (100 samples) — PASS. Closing customer-facing mitigation. We'll still follow up with a technical write-up for affected customers.

omar_eng: Adding this to the 1.2 post-merge checklist: include tokenization regression tests and safety-threshold verification.

lucy_support: Sending final note to Ledgerly now. :white_check_mark:"
